newsitem.title: USA: Most US stock index futures end lackluster day up.
newsitem.headline: Most US stock index futures end lackluster day up.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures ended a lackluster session slightly higher, with most traders expecting rangebound activity through the week.
They said the U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding auction this week was likely to keep U.S. T-bonds on the defensive and thus contain momentum in the Standard & Poor's 500 futures pit.
Some also said September S&Ps were likely to stall in front of next week's batch of U.S. inflationary reports.
"There's just not a lot to go on right now," one S&P futures floor trader said.
Volume was exceptionally light, estimated by floor traders at 49,000 contracts.

September S&Ps sputtered to the upside and to the downside, but failed to find momentum after the results of the first leg of the Treasury's auction this afternoon and U.S. June leading economic indicators this morning.
Regardless, traders are looking for September S&Ps to grind higher and re-test the all-time high of 963.90.
One trader said 970.00 is an upside objective.
"It's more of a mental objective than chart objective," he said.
September S&Ps are expected to fall no lower than 950.00, he said.
Fair value is at 4.48 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs at 5.80 points over and arbitrage sell programs at 3.90 points over, floor traders said.

At the end of pit trade, September S&Ps were up 1.10 points at 956.50, KCBT Value Lines were up 3.80 at 846.50, new composite was up 0.10 at 494.95, Nikkeis were down 280 at 19,480, Nasdaq 100s were up 12.35 at 1,143.85 and Russell 2000s were 4.75 higher at 421.75. ((Chicago Derivatives Desk, 312-408-8750))
